notes.title: Major Update: Original text-heavy and Visualized modes now available
notes.content:
[p]Fellow vampires! With the latest patch now live, players have a choice of which mode of the game to play.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/27d0744f31ca9426bfbe39815e907f3851898e1f.png"][/img][/p][p]Those you care about, you let them eat.[b]

Original/Textual:[/b] The Original version of the game in which combat and feeding were based on narrative choices, with the game play following a presentation similar to what a game master would narrate. This mode is recommended for new players and for those who want to experience the narration in full, at all stages.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Original/Abbreviated[/b]: Same as the Original version of the game in which combat and feeding were based on narrative choices, but with the following change: once a situation has been encountered and described, the next time the same situation occurs, the narration is substituted by a short notification of the outcome.  There is somewhat less reading and clicking but at the cost of no longer being able to see a description again.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/6e388cc08758e727251e10cd9b59b018332300e5.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Once in [b]Original[/b] mode, you can ask the fortune teller to switch between [b]Textual[/b] and [b]Abbreviated[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][b]Alternative:[/b] The Alternative version replaces feeding and combat with interactive elements. Hunting and feeding take faster and the combat rules are different, even though the game balance is similar. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/f8b5b0ebeb070efa5f49115b165f500147bf103e.gif"][/img][/p][p]In all modes, the game is balanced to be beatable with a character above level 5.  The combat perks that appear at levels 4 and higher in the Alternative version are different from those in the Original, offering new strategies.  Nevertheless, you still need them to have a chance in combat. Having a knife on you still affects one attack in the Original version and offers no combat bonuses in the Alternative. All quests remain unchanged. [/p][p][/p][p]The Alternative mode can be treated as a separate game with the same story and additional assets.[/p]

tags.feature: Original/Textual: The Original version of the game in which combat and feeding were based on narrative choices, with the game play following a presentation similar to what a game master would narrate. This mode is recommended for new players and for those who want to experience the narration in full, at all stages.

Original/Abbreviated: Same as the Original version of the game in which combat and feeding were based on narrative choices, but with the following change: once a situation has been encountered and described, the next time the same situation occurs, the narration is substituted by a short notification of the outcome. There is somewhat less reading and clicking but at the cost of no longer being able to see a description again.

Alternative: The Alternative version replaces feeding and combat with interactive elements. Hunting and feeding take faster and the combat rules are different, even though the game balance is similar.

notes.title: Vampirii 1.5 is now live!
notes.content:
[h2]Fellow vampires![/h2]

I am pleased to announce that Vampirii 1.5 is now live! To a certain extent, outside the quests and storyline, it is a new game. I invite you to try it, whether for the first time or as a returning player, and if you like what you see, feel free to leave a kind word and let your friends know.

[h3]What has changed?[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/ee581c9a52ccd437bd59d4f8be5f7f117bc6e660.gif[/img]

[h3]Combat overhaul[/h3]
[list]
[*]     The menu choices are gone, replaced with an interactive system.
[*]     You can choose which enemy to attack.
[*]     Enemies fight back during their turn, using their weapons.
[*]     To keep the overall difficulty close to the original, there has been some rebalancing. All human 
 enemies now have 4 hit points. The dice-dependent chance for an enemy to dodge your attack is gone. In Vampirii 1.5, there is only one character—a potential ally—who retains the ability to dodge.
[*]     Health regeneration per turn, if a character has it, now applies in all battles.
[*]     Loot drops dynamically, and there is no recap screen. This allows for some hit-and-run strategies.
[*]     The “rage” and “see prey” modes are gone. You will have access to new perks starting from level 4
[*]     You are capable of reloading and firing the launcher during the same turn in the form of two separate actions.
[*]     The close combat/distant combat system, already present in the earlier version, has been made more explicit. If you don’t close the distance yourself, enemies advance on you each turn.
[*]     Your basic attack is weak in the beginning. Don’t expect to win many brawls before reaching levels 4-5. This is consistent with the difficulty in the original.
[*]     Like the original, you can bring one of three possible allies to the final encounter (or try it solo), which has been rebuilt entirely. If an ally can use a launcher, they will fire each turn, as long as you have provided ammunition in advance.
[*]     At a later stage of the game, there is a UI indicator for how much of a “certain challenge” you will be facing.
[/list]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/1ebd52bb7c04742a613b5e2811b43038b8e3c97d.gif[/img]
[h3]Feeding overhaul[/h3]

[list]
[*]     The menu choices are gone, replaced with an interactive system.
[*]     When you approach a house, the available points of interest will be gently highlighted. Some become available when their prerequisites are met. For example, an open window on the second floor will activate only if you have enough blood points for the jump.
[*]     Once inside, you will see an interactive floor plan. Proceed to your heart’s content.
[*]     There are now 16 human targets on whom you can feed. Some are more pleasing to the eye than others. They appear depending on the locale. When prowling a home, you won’t run into someone from the Alleys, and vice versa. Similarly, the abandoned area has its own cohort of sleeping denizens.
[*]     The “feed for one point” option is gone. Now you choose between “feed and let live” and “drain to death.” You can figure out which is which.
[*]     Feeding on animals is interactive in the same way as normal combat. When the opportunity to feed on an animal arises, special buttons appear for the new options. Certain animals may need to be “softened” first. Like the original, if you kill too many animals, they will become less frequent for a while.
[/list]

[h3]Other changes[/h3]

[list]
[*]     The coven that you can join shortly after you get your feet wet no longer provides free clothing.
[*]     A diary becomes accessible after you taste blood for the first time. To strike a balance between offering no information at all and turning the game into a checklist, the diary updates as you progress with useful tips and information, without becoming a quest-by-quest log.
[*]     Text and image edits.
[*]     Added many new SFX and changed/replaced some old ones.
[*]     Added combat VFX.
[*]     Added some new images.
[/list]

For the best experience, you may want to start a new game. Older saves should work from any lair, but it is not guaranteed.

[b]Have fun![/b]

notes.title: Version 1.1
notes.content:
[h1] Changes to hunting and feeding feedback[/h1]

* When facing a situation for the first time while prowling residential areas, the player will see the full text describing the scene and the outcome of any action chosen. When the same situation occurs again later, the description will be omitted (unless it is very short) and the outcome will be presented either directly by loading the next portion or in a very short message that indicates the outcome. For example, when trying to enter a home through the window after a scenario has already been experienced, a successful outcome will bring the inside content right away and a negative outcome will bring a message, such as "it doesn't open."

* Also, the comments before and after feeding were removed, expect for the very first instances. While they will be missed, these comments ran the risk of becoming repetitive and simply resulting in having to click extra times. If players desire that comments come back in some form, they may be made a randomized rare occurrence.

The final and fastest feeding grounds do not involve entering and breaking and thus received no changes. These are already "fast enough" in both leveling and sustenance.

Happy hunting!

notes.title: Vampirii 1.1: Changes in Hunting and Feeding feedback
notes.content:
[h1]  What is new in Version 1.1? Changes and the reasons behind them.[/h1]

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45079568/27d0744f31ca9426bfbe39815e907f3851898e1f.png[/img]

Fellow vampires,

The "hunt and feed" cycle before "getting out of town" in Vampirii faces a challenge when it comes to meeting two goals at once: 

* providing a narrative experience that approximates that of a table top game with some unnecessary complexities removed;  and
*  keeping the pace of the game such that players can spend[u] enough time[/u] to feel both immersed and invested in the story and the character's "life" as a vampire, [u]but not so much time[/u] that a mechanic would become to feel repetitive. 

Hunting and feeding are both core mechanics that balance the rest of the questing, provide the fuel for leveling up and fighting, and keep our character grounded in reality regarding his new existence.   

Depending on the life story background, the player faces different options and chances of success when negotiating windows, garage doors, roofs, and places where keys might be hidden.  While the narrative pool of scenarios and outcomes offers enough variety (including 1/20 and 1/10 occurrences while attempting to beak in), sooner or later a player has seen all the outcomes.

[h3]To address this issue, the following changes were made:[/h3]

* When facing a situation for the first time while prowling residential areas, the player will see the full text describing the scene and the outcome of any action chosen.  When the same situation occurs again later, the description will be omitted (unless it is very short) and the outcome will be presented either directly by loading the next portion or in a very short message that indicates the outcome.  For example, when trying to enter a home through the window after a scenario has already been experienced, a successful outcome will bring the inside content right away and a negative outcome will bring a message, such as "it doesn't open." 

* Also, the comments before and after feeding were removed, expect for the very first instances. While they will be missed, these comments ran the risk of becoming repetitive and simply resulting in having to click extra times. If players desire that comments come back in some form, they may be made a randomized rare occurrence.
 
The final and fastest feeding grounds do not involve entering and breaking and thus received no changes. These are already "fast enough" in both leveling and sustenance. 

Happy hunting!
